newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end lower on foreign selling.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end lower on foreign selling.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended lower, led by leading supermarket chain Carulla, after coming under pressure from selling by foreign investment funds, brokers said.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index slipped 0.27 percent to end at 16,686.73 on trading volume of about 1.3 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB fell 0.17 percent, closing at 1,066.50 on above average volume nearly three billion pesos.
"There were big cross-trades involving foreign funds that wanted to sell," one broker said. "Some shares couldn't be sustained because funds weren't out there buying either."
Carulla took the biggest hit by far. It fell 10 percent in Medellin to close at 3,600 pesos per share on deals that saw 10.8 million pesos of stock in the retailer change hands.
Investment analysts have said Carulla looks vulnerable in Colombia's increasingly competitive food retailing sector.
Corporacion Financiera del Valle was also hit by foreign fund selling, although not as badly as Carulla. It fell 1.52 percent in Bogota to close at 2,265 pesos per share.
"Neither one of these shares has been actively traded lately," one broker told Reuters. "When someone goes out to sell, prices take a beating, especially if there's no demand."

Other losers included Bancoquia, a bank that had posted steep gains over the previous two sessions on rumors about its expected takeover by Spain's Banco Santander. Bancoquia's losses were limited to 0.18 percent, however, and it closed at an even 3,300 pesos per share in Bogota and Medellin.

Actively traded brewing giant Bavaria SA also closed lower, ending down 0.10 percent at 6,803 pesos per share. Cement maker Cementos Argos fell 1.37 percent, meanwhile, ending at 7,900 pesos per share.
